verdict.rationale: Rootly's own docs say it offers private status pages alongside public ones. They also say status pages can serve internal stakeholders as well as external customers and partners, which covers the core idea of internal, non-public pages. The pack does not document how access to private pages is controlled, and it does not show pages scoped to specific customers. missing for 10: documented access-control mechanism (e.g. SSO, password, IP or email allowlists), customer-specific audience scoping, independent or hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As an engineering leader, I can run private or internal status pages with access control for customer-specific or employee-only audiences

citations.quote: Rootly has two types of status pages available: public status pages and private status pages.
Status pages allow you to quickly communicate information about the health of your services and applications to internal stakeholders and external customers.
Status pages let you share the health of your systems with the people who depend on them, from internal teams to customers and partners.
